quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Tagrisso plus Orpathys demonstrated statistically (08-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Positive high-level results from the global SAFFRON Phase III trial: Tagrisso (osimertinib, 80mg once daily) plus Orpathys (savolitinib, 300mg twice daily) showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in both progression-free survival (primary endpoint) and overall survival (key secondary endpoint) versus doublet platinum-based chemotherapy in 338 patients with EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with high MET overexpression or amplification whose disease progressed after 1st- or 2nd-line Tagrisso. The trial ran in 230 centres across 29 countries, with patients prospectively selected using the high MET cut-offs identified in the SAVANNAH Phase II trial (IHC and FISH tests); safety was consistent with each medicine's known profile, and the data will be presented at a forthcoming medical meeting and shared with global regulatory authorities. The combination is already approved in China (SACHI Phase III) and has a temporary authorisation in Switzerland (SAVANNAH). The company estimates 34% of tumours develop high MET overexpression or amplification after progression on a third-generation EGFR-TKI. Orpathys is jointly developed with HUTCHMED and commercialised by AstraZeneca. Tagrisso is approved as monotherapy in more than 120 countries and with chemotherapy in more than 80 countries, and has treated more than one million patients. The company calls SAFFRON the first global Phase III trial to show significant PFS and OS benefits in this setting (company claim).
